BiblicalUsage: Agnoia is ignorance — the state of not knowing. Peter tells the Jews they crucified Christ through ignorance; Paul tells Athens that God winked at the times of this ignorance, but now commands all men to repent; he says the Gentiles are darkened through the ignorance in them; and he tells believers not to fashion themselves after their former lusts in their ignorance. The word always marks the before — the life before knowing God — and the gospel is what ends it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word is the hinge of the gospel's call. Ignorance was winked at for a time, but now God commands repentance — and the ignorance that once excused us is the very thing Christ came to end, by making Himself known.
